Abstract:

Nature has always been an excellent source of inspiration for solving complex engineering and healthcare challenges. In recent years, biomimicry-inspired nanobioengineering has gained significant attention for developing next-generation biomedical technologies by adapting natural structures, functions, and mechanisms into advanced nanoscale systems. This talk will present recent developments in translational nanobioengineering, including bioinspired nanomaterials, biosensors, tissue engineering strategies, and targeted therapeutic platforms for healthcare applications. Particular focus will be given to how biomimetic concepts combined with nanotechnology can lead to smart, efficient, and clinically relevant solutions for disease diagnosis and treatment. The presentation will also highlight current challenges, translational opportunities, and future prospects for bringing laboratory innovations closer to real-world biomedical applications. Biography Dr. Gopinath Packirisamy is a Professor at the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee and the A.S. Arya Institute Chair Professor, internationally recognised for his contributions to biomedical nanotechnology. He has also served as Associate Dean of Academic Affairs and Head of the Centre for Nanotechnology. His research focuses on nanomaterial-based platforms for biosensing, tissue engineering, and theranostics. He has published over 180 high-impact papers and holds 36 patents, including 20 granted, with a successful technology transfer. His work has received over 10,000 citations (h-index 57). He has led several nationally and internationally funded projects and received prestigious honours, including the Tata Innovation Fellowship by DBT, Government of India. He is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry and the Royal Society of Biology, United Kingdom.
